definition: A forward is a physically settled contract that is economically similar to a futures contract but is negotiated directly (bilaterally/OTC) between two counterparties rather than cleared on an exchange.
core_idea: Forwards give traders the same ability as futures to lock in a future price, location, and time, but without exchange clearing — trading customization for counterparty credit exposure.
key_points: Because there is no clearinghouse, each party bears direct credit risk that the other side will fail to perform.
In theory forwards can be fully customized for illiquid or unique products, but in practice most are standardized, following terms similar to futures.
relationships: Forwards are the bilateral counterpart to exchange-cleared futures; an OTC clearing service can convert a forward into a future by inserting the exchange as counterparty.
trading_implications: Choosing a forward over a future trades exchange credit protection for contract customization (location, volume, delivery schedule).
caveats: Treating forwards as interchangeable with futures in terms of counterparty risk — forwards carry direct bilateral credit risk that futures do not.
